title: You Are Not What You Feel — Jeremiah 17:9
paragraphs: You Are Not What You Feel — Jeremiah 17:9
You are not what you feel.

Until Jeremiah 17:9 cuts through the fog:
“The heart is deceitful above all things, and desperately sick; who can understand it?”
That means your feelings can be loud… and still be lying.

Your heart can call lust “love.”
It can call rebellion “freedom.”
It can call bitterness “discernment.”
It can call fear “wisdom.”
And if you build your life on every emotion that rises in you, you will worship your impulses and call it authenticity.

God never told you to be led by your feelings.
He told you to be transformed by His truth.

Feelings are real.
They are just not reliable masters.

That ache in your chest?
That panic?
That craving?
That shame?

It may describe your battle.
It does not define your identity.

In Christ, you are not named by what surges through you in a weak moment.
You are named by what Jesus did for you at the cross.

The world says, “Follow your heart.”
Jesus says, “Follow Me.”

One leads deeper into confusion.
The other leads dead people into life.

So when your emotions preach louder than Scripture, do not bow.
Bring them under the Word.
Bring them to the feet of Christ.
Bring them into the light.

Because salvation is not found in trusting yourself more.
It is found in repenting of self-trust and resting in Jesus alone.

You are not what you feel.
You are who God says you are—if you belong to Christ.
